answer: A Barolo carries its vineyard in its strontium: the vine drinks 87Sr/86Sr from its soil as it lies, and the ratio holds across vintages. A ballot must do the same: claim one vine and press a pigment sample at the tide's pulse. Verifiers match it against the terroir atlas: Douro 0.7130-0.7175, Lisbon 0.706-0.709. Each assay costs $190 and two lab days. A farm claiming 10,000 vines dies by the atlas check: all its samples read 0.7071, so 9,999 claims miss their plots, are rejected, and their $25 bonds burn — $249,975 gone, plus $1.9M in assays and 20,000 lab-days. One vine, one fingerprint.
